body: Wario World is Treasure's GameCube action platformer about recovering Wario's castle and fortune from the Black Jewel. The gem transforms his possessions into monsters and sends him through a succession of colourful worlds. Wario responds with punches, throws and the heavy movements expected of a hero whose main concern remains his own wealth. The adventure puts close physical combat beside platforming, allowing an enemy to become something that can be lifted and used rather than simply removed with a single jump.

Wario can grab opponents, spin them around, throw them or drive them into the ground. Those actions affect groups and nearby objects, making position part of deciding which move is useful next. Environmental items can also be handled as weapons. The character's weight becomes an advantage when a heavy landing or powerful throw opens the space around him. Fighting therefore contributes to the game's comic identity: the same greedy figure crossing the platforms can abruptly turn a small opponent into the tool needed to deal with several others.

Trapdoors lead to separate platforming and puzzle challenges containing treasure, giving exploration a role beside the more direct action. Rescuing Spritelings also affects Wario's reward at the end of the journey. Treasure developed the game for a 2003 release, bringing its experience in inventive action systems to Nintendo's unruly protagonist. The shorter campaign concentrates on a recognisable personality expressed through movement. Wario does not merely look heavy and impatient; the player repeatedly uses that weight and impatience to break through whatever has been placed in front of him.
story_headings: Pick up the enemy and change the fight
